title: No MCP protocol implementation — plain Go library, not an MCP server
evidence: grep for jsonrpc|stdio|RegisterTool|modelcontextprotocol|tools/list|tools/call across *.go = 0 hits (only the module name and a struct literally named MCPServer match 'mcp'). go.mod (all 3 lines) declares zero dependencies — no MCP/JSON-RPC SDK. server/server.go:12 MCPServer is a plain struct; main.go:37-48 constructs it and calls its methods directly in exampleQueries(). No transport, no tool registration, no tool schemas — cannot be connected to an LLM as an MCP server.
suggestion: Add a JSON-RPC-over-stdio transport and register the query methods as MCP tools with input schemas (e.g. via an MCP Go SDK), or hand-roll initialize/tools/list/tools/call handlers.

title: Team statistics compute goals for/against incorrectly for away matches
evidence: server/server.go:88-90 unconditionally does stats.GoalsFor += m.HomeGoals; stats.GoalsAgainst += m.AwayGoals for every match, so for away matches goals-for/against are swapped. W/L/D counts (server/server.go:92-108) correctly branch on isHome/isAway. The sibling functions CalculateStandings (server/server.go:215-218) and GetHeadToHead (server/server.go:150-152) get the away swap right, confirming this is a bug, not a modeling choice. TestGetTeamStatistics (main_test.go:150-186) only prints Matches/Wins and never asserts GoalsFor/GoalsAgainst, so the bug is unexercised.
suggestion: In GetTeamStatistics, when isAway add m.AwayGoals to GoalsFor and m.HomeGoals to GoalsAgainst (mirror the branch already used in CalculateStandings), and add a test asserting goals for/against for a team's away matches.

title: TestGetTeamStatistics asserts nothing about goals
evidence: main_test.go:150-186 calls GetTeamStatistics but only fmt.Printf's Matches/Wins/WinRate and checks err; no assertion on GoalsFor/GoalsAgainst, so the away-goals swap in server/server.go:88-90 passes tests silently.
suggestion: Assert expected goals for/against on a small fixture that includes at least one away match for the team.

title: Query/data layer is complete and idiomatic apart from the MCP transport
evidence: data/loader.go loads all 6 CSVs from data/kaggle/ (loader.go:213-533) with team-name normalization (loader.go:170-211); server/server.go exposes 30+ query methods (matches by team/season/competition/date-range, standings, head-to-head, aggregates, player search). Only the MCP protocol wrapper (R1) is absent.
suggestion: Wrapping the existing methods in an MCP tool layer would satisfy R1 with little change to the query logic.
